findings.title: ?tab=adoption URL silently enters custom-dashboard path
findings.problem: isAdoptionTab was removed without adding a redirect or exclusion guard for the 'adoption' value. isCustomDashboard (tab && !isInsightsTab && !isLeaderboardTab) now evaluates true when tab='adoption', assigning dashboardId='adoption' and forwarding it to AnalyticsDashboard with no matching tab entry.
findings.impact: Any user navigating to a bookmarked ?tab=adoption URL gets a broken analytics page: a spurious 'Edit Dashboard' button for a non-existent custom dashboard with id 'adoption', and AnalyticsDashboard rendering with no active tab panel — blank or errored content.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit redirect when the incoming tab value is not a recognised AnalyticsDashboard enum member (e.g. a useEffect that calls setSearchParams({ tab: AnalyticsDashboardType.insights }) when tab is not insights, leaderboard, or a known custom dashboard id), or extend the isCustomDashboard guard to require the tab value to exist in the loaded dashboards list.

findings.title: No replacement test for broken ?tab=adoption regression
findings.problem: The test 'should NOT show Edit Dashboard button when tab is adoption' was removed with no replacement covering the new behavior where tab=adoption produces isCustomDashboard=true and a spurious Edit Dashboard button — the same broken path confirmed in CR-001.
findings.impact: The regression introduced by CR-001 has no automated coverage. Future refactors to isCustomDashboard or tab-routing logic can silently worsen the adoption URL behavior without any gate catching it.
findings.recommendation: Add a test asserting that navigating to ?tab=adoption redirects to the insights tab (or the expected fallback) and does not render 'Edit Dashboard'. This test should fail until CR-001 is also resolved.

findings.title: Removed adoption route has no redirect registered
findings.problem: The route /settings/administration/ai-adoption-config was deleted. No redirect or catch-all is registered in its place. React Router finds no match and renders blank content under the root layout; the root ErrorBoundary handles JS errors, not unmatched routes.
findings.impact: Users or automated integrations navigating to the removed path receive a blank page with no error message or navigation cue. The silent blank is worse than an explicit 404.
findings.recommendation: Register a redirect from /settings/administration/ai-adoption-config to /settings/administration using react-router's redirect route config or a <Navigate> element, so existing bookmarks land on the administration page rather than a blank screen.

findings.title: Dead overview field remains in Analytics interface and clearState
findings.problem: overview: SummariesResponse | null persists in the Analytics interface and is reset in clearState(), but its sole writer (fetchAiAdoptionOverview) was deleted in this change. No component reads or writes this field.
findings.impact: Dead interface field misleads future contributors about the live store shape. clearState() performs a no-op reset on it. Signals incomplete cleanup and may cause confusion during future store modifications.
findings.recommendation: Remove the overview field from the Analytics interface declaration and from the clearState() body in src/store/analytics.ts.

findings.title: Dead exported drill-down functions still make live AI-adoption API calls
findings.problem: openUserEngagementDrillDown, closeUserEngagementDrillDown, fetchUserEngagementUsers, and equivalent assetReusability* exports remain in analytics.ts after all consuming components were deleted. openUserEngagementDrillDown sets isOpen=true on userEngagementDrillDown and POSTs to v1/analytics/ai-adoption-user-engagement/users. The store state and types (UserEngagementDrillDownState, AssetReusabilityDrillDownState) are also retained in the interface.
findings.impact: If any external caller or future developer invokes these exports the drill-down store state is permanently opened with no UI path to close it, and live POST requests are sent to AI-adoption endpoints that are no longer part of the product. Dead exported functions from a removed feature are a latent liability.
findings.recommendation: Remove userEngagementDrillDown and assetReusabilityDrillDown from the Analytics interface and store proxy, delete all exported drill-down helpers (openUserEngagementDrillDown, closeUserEngagementDrillDown, fetchUserEngagementUsers, openAssetReusabilityDrillDown, and related assetReusability helpers), and remove their type declarations from analytics.ts.

findings.title: Orphaned localStorage key not cleared on app initialisation
findings.problem: aiAdoptionConfigStorage.ts was deleted without adding a one-time cleanup step. The 'codemie-ai-adoption-config' localStorage key persists in every returning user's browser with no code path to remove it.
findings.impact: Stale adoption config data accumulates in users' localStorage indefinitely. If the key name is reused for a different feature it will be pre-populated with stale AI adoption data, producing subtle and hard-to-trace initialisation bugs.
findings.recommendation: Add localStorage.removeItem('codemie-ai-adoption-config') in app initialisation — for example in src/main.tsx or the appInfoStore initializer — so the orphaned key is cleared for all users on the first load after deployment.
